title: Improving transition to IPv6-only via RFC8925 and IPv4 DNS Interventions : A case study in implementing an IPv6-only testbed which informs IPv4-only clients why internet access is unavailable
problem: Legacy IPv4-only clients cannot access IPv6-only networks and need graceful notification about protocol incompatibility. Organizations struggle to sunset IPv4 infrastructure despite IPv4 address exhaustion and government mandates for IPv6 transition.
motivation: Improving IPv6-only network deployment strategies is critical as Federally Funded Research and Development Centers face challenges completing IPv6 transition despite mandates and address shortage.
method: The approach leverages RFC8925 to allow clients to disable IPv4 while retaining connectivity via RFC6145 translation algorithm, and implements poisoned IPv4 DNS records to gracefully inform IPv4-only clients of incompatibility. The method was deployed on SC24v6 wireless network with design provisions to minimize impact on RFC8925-compliant and dual-stack clients.
key_novelty: Using poisoned IPv4 DNS records as a graceful notification mechanism to inform IPv4-only clients why they cannot access IPv6-only networks.
contributions: Practical implementation demonstrating RFC8925 for IPv4-to-IPv6 protocol negotiation
Poisoned DNS record technique for gracefully notifying incompatible IPv4-only clients
Real-world case study from SC24v6 wireless network deployment
Method design to minimize disruption to RFC8925-compliant and dual-stack clients
limitations: Limitations specific to FFRDC deployments and scalability constraints not discussed.
primary_theme: IPv6-only network transition via DNS interventions
